rows.jp: 教室に来ると、誰もいなかった。
rows.en: The classroom was empty when I arrived.

ghs.en: When I went into the classroom no one was there.

rows.jp: いつも自席でむっつりしている冬子の姿はなかった。
rows.en: Touko was nowhere to be seen, though she normally sat at her desk in sullen silence.

ghs.en: There was no trace of that Touko and her persistent gloom at her desk.

rows.jp: 鞄から原稿用紙を取り出す。
rows.en: I took the manuscript pages from my bag.

ghs.en: I take out the manuscript's paper from my bag.
ghs.assessment: The source names manuscript paper as a type of paper. The possessive makes the paper belong to a manuscript rather than identify the stationery he takes from his bag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'manuscript paper.'

rows.jp: 原稿は一晩でできてしまった。
rows.en: I had finished the entire script in a single night.

ghs.en: I'd managed to finish the script overnight.

rows.jp: さっそく見せてＯＫをもらおう。
rows.en: Time to show it to Misato and get her approval.

ghs.en: I wanna go show this right away, so it can receive the OK.

rows.jp: 疑惑の視線に出迎えられた。

ghs.en: I was welcomed by a distrustful gaze.

rows.jp: 「なぜあなたは胸元をガードしているのです？」
rows.en: “And why are you guarding your chest?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why are you guarding your upper chest?"

rows.jp: 「あの、昨日のこと、わたしよくおぼえてないんですけど」
rows.en: “Um... I don’t remember much about yesterday.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Uhm, it is about what happened yesterday, I do not remember it well..."

ghs.assessment: The source agrees that she naturally would not remember, roughly 'I figured as much.' The English instead asks a skeptical question and reverses the reply's speech function.
ghs.remedy: Use an agreeing response such as 'I thought so.'

ghs.en: Misato: "Wh-, what if I, what if I...?"

rows.jp: うつむいて、懊悩(おうのう)している。
rows.en: She hung her head in anguish.

ghs.en: She hangs her head in shame and, oh no!, grows anguished.
ghs.assessment: The source says she hangs her head and agonizes. The English adds shame as a specific cause and inserts a jaunty 'oh no!' that undercuts the described anguish.
ghs.remedy: Describe her hanging her head in anguish without the added aside.

highlights.text: in shame and, oh no!, grows anguished

rows.jp: しかし胸を覆った腕は、微塵も揺るがない。
rows.en: Yet her arms stayed locked over her chest.

ghs.en: However, the arm covering the chest does not shake by a single atom.

rows.jp: 「それよりこっちに行きましょう」
rows.en: “Never mind that. Let’s move over here.”

rows.jp: 先輩の手首をつかんで、引く。
rows.en: I took her by the wrist and pulled.

ghs.en: I grab Senpai's wrist and pull.

ghs.assessment: The source says the flustered senior cries out. The English places the adjective and verb before the subject without a grammatical inversion structure.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai cries out in a panic.'

rows.jp: 頭の中で、羊が一頭、草むらに突っ込んだ。
rows.en: In my mind, a lone sheep dove headfirst into the grass.

ghs.en: Inside of my head a sheep, just one, diving into a thicket.

rows.jp: 「スケープゴートは、いやです」
rows.en: “I don’t want to be a scapegoat.”

ghs.en: Misato: "It is scapegoat, that is bad!"
ghs.assessment: The source says she does not want to be made a scapegoat. The English labels an unspecified thing 'scapegoat' and calls it bad, losing the first-person refusal.
ghs.remedy: Say 'I don't want to be a scapegoat.'

highlights.text: It is scapegoat, that is bad

ghs.en: Taichi: "I do not like them myself."
ghs.assessment: The source replies that he would not want that either. The plural pronoun has no antecedent and changes shared aversion to the situation into disliking people or things.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I wouldn't want that either.'

highlights.text: I do not like them myself

rows.jp: 「気をつけないといけませんねっ」

ghs.en: Misato: "Not paying attention is out of the question!"

rows.jp: 「でも俺、先輩をスケープゴートにしたかったわけじゃなくて、日陰に移動したかっただけなんすけど」
rows.en: “But I wasn’t trying to make you a scapegoat. I was trying to move you into the shade.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But me, I was not trying to make scapegoat of you, Senpai, I just wanted us to move to the shade."
ghs.assessment: The source says he was not trying to make her a scapegoat. The English drops the required article before the predicate noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'make a scapegoat of you.'

rows.jp: 「あっ、そうですね、じゃあそうしましょう」

ghs.en: Misato: "Ah, I see now, well then let us."
ghs.assessment: The source accepts the suggestion and says they should move. The English ends after the auxiliary 'let us' without naming or substituting for the action.
ghs.remedy: Complete the response, such as 'Then let's do that.'

rows.en: She was coming apart at the seams.

rows.jp: 「ところで先輩、昨日はお酒飲んでましたね」
rows.en: “By the way, you were drinking yesterday.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Anyway, Senpai, yesterday you were drinking alcohol, were you."
ghs.assessment: The source matter-of-factly reminds her that she drank yesterday. The English appends a positive tag to a positive statement, producing a malformed confirmation question.
ghs.remedy: Use a statement or a correctly formed tag question.

rows.jp: 「まさかわたし……酔って……たいへんなことを？」
rows.en: “D-did I... get drunk and do something terrible?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Could it be that... drunk... I did something really bad?"
ghs.assessment: The source line is the senior's alarmed first-person question about what she may have done while drunk. The English speaker label assigns her words to the narrator.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to the senior.

rows.jp: 「ええ、それはもう口にはできないような破廉恥プレイを」
rows.en: “Oh, yes. A display of depravity too obscene to describe.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, that was the kind of shameless playact one should simply never again describe."
ghs.assessment: The source claims she engaged in unspeakably shameless play. 'Playact' makes it mere pretending, while 'never again describe' adds prior description and future prohibition not present in the line.
ghs.remedy: Call it shameless conduct too indecent to put into words.

highlights.text: playact one should simply never again describe

rows.jp: 先輩の目が横長の『×』マークになった。
rows.en: Her eyes flattened into a pair of X’s.

ghs.en: Senpai's eyes became an [><] mark in landscape orientation.

rows.jp: 「でもご安心を。僕がうまく処理して、人目につかないよう片づけておきました」
rows.en: “But don’t worry. I took care of it and cleaned everything up before anyone could see.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But be at ease! This harmless young boy skillfully dealt with it, it has been cleaned up so that the public eye will never notice!"

rows.jp: 「……ああ、そうだったの……どうも、ありがとう」

ghs.en: Misato: "...ahhh, so you did... thank you, very much."

rows.jp: 釈然としないものを残しつつも、先輩は頭を下げた。
rows.en: The explanation plainly failed to satisfy her, but she bowed all the same.

ghs.en: Something she is unsatisfied about still remained, and Senpai hung her head.
ghs.assessment: The source says she bows her head in thanks despite lingering uncertainty. 'Hung her head' conventionally signals shame or dejection and changes the gesture's function.
ghs.remedy: Say that she bowed her head.

rows.jp: 「でもわたし、いったいどんな醜態を……」
rows.en: “But what kind of disgraceful spectacle did I make of myself...?”

ghs.en: Misato: "But me, what sort of disgraceful conduct..."

ghs.assessment: The source asks whether she wants to hear the details. The English asks whether she herself is asking, reversing the direction of the offered information.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Want to hear?'

rows.jp: 「なんでしたら責任取りましょうか？」
rows.en: “If you’d like, I could always make an honest woman of you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Will you take responsibility, whatever it is?"
ghs.assessment: The source has the narrator offer to take responsibility if she wishes. The English demands that she take responsibility, reversing the subject and intent.
ghs.remedy: Have the narrator ask whether he should take responsibility.

rows.jp: 今度は目が点になった。

ghs.en: This time her eyes turn into dots from the shock.

rows.jp: 「いや、聞いちゃったら、そういう気分になるかなって」
rows.en: “I thought hearing it might put you in that sort of mood.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nah, if you're asking, then who knows if you really will..."
ghs.assessment: The source explains that hearing the story might put her in the mood to want him to take responsibility. The English changes hearing into asking and leaves the prospective feeling unstated.
ghs.remedy: Say that he wondered whether hearing it would put her in that mood.

highlights.text: if you're asking, then who knows if you really will

rows.jp: 「いや、冷静に考えるとたいしたことじゃないんです」
rows.en: “But really, if you think about it, it wasn’t such a big deal.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nah, if I think about it calmly, it was not that big of a mess."

ghs.assessment: The repeated source question again offers to tell her the details. The English again reverses the exchange into asking whether she is requesting something.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Do you want to hear?'

rows.jp: ずいぶんと長い時間、先輩は寄り目で考えていた。
rows.en: Misato spent an impressively long time thinking cross-eyed.

ghs.en: For a considerably long while Senpai mulled over with crossed eyes.
Taichi: "That was really a big mess."
ghs.assessment: The source begins reassuring her that it really was not a serious matter. The English removes the negation and tells her it was a major mess, reversing polarity just before the fabricated story.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the negative reassurance: 'It really wasn't anything serious.'

highlights.text: That was really a big mess

rows.jp: 「あそこのアンテナ用の針金を使って、ちょっと全裸リンボーダンス撮影会をこっち向きで」
rows.en: “You did a naked limbo photo shoot using that antenna wire—facing straight at me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Using some of the wiring of that antenna over yonder, you did a little naked limbo dance photo-shoot facing my direction."
Flop, and she sinks hard to the floor.

rows.jp: 「拝啓、春眠の候、その後いかがお過ごしでしょうか……」
rows.en: “Dear Sir or Madam: I trust the drowsy days of spring find you well...”

ghs.en: Misato: "Dear sir, I hope that things have been well since the month with those sweet small clumsy feet..."
ghs.assessment: The source parodies a formal seasonal letter greeting about spring drowsiness. The English invents a month characterized by small clumsy feet and loses the seasonal phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use a mock-formal springtime greeting appropriate to a letter.

highlights.text: month with those sweet small clumsy feet

rows.jp: 架空の手紙を読み出した。
rows.en: She began reading an imaginary letter.

ghs.en: She reads out an Imaginary letter.

ghs.assessment: The source urges her to pull herself together. The isolated adjective 'steadfast' describes a trait rather than functioning as the intended encouragement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Pull yourself together, Senpai.'

rows.jp: 「……これ以上、人生が最悪になるなんて思ってませんでした……」
rows.en: “...I never imagined my life could sink any lower...”

ghs.en: Misato: "...I did not believe that living could worsen any more than this..."

rows.jp: 「もしかして、家に帰ってらっしゃらない？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Could it perhaps be that you have not returned home yet?"

rows.jp: 「じゃあ、今は……目覚めたときのままなのですか？」
rows.en: “Then you’re still... exactly as you were when you woke up?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then, right now... you are as you woke up?"
Second time, a bob of the head.

rows.jp: ごくり、と唾を飲み込む。
薄手の透けやすいシャツの下っ。
服のッッッ下はッッッッッッ裸ッッッッッッッ！！
rows.en: UNDER!! HER CLOTHES!!!!!! SHE WAS NAKED!!!!!!!!

rows.jp: ……って、そんなこと言ったら、世界中の女子っ娘が服の下は裸である。
rows.en: ...Though if you put it that way, every single girl in the world was naked under her clothes.

ghs.en: ...wait, if I put it that way, then throughout the world there's girlettes naked under their clothes.

rows.jp: ま、要するに……ノーブラなわけだ。
rows.en: Meaning... she wasn’t wearing a bra.

ghs.en: Well, in other words... she's currently going no-bra.

rows.jp: 先輩、大きめだからなぁ。
rows.en: And Misato was on the busty side.

ghs.en: And because Senpai's are biiit large,

rows.jp: シャツが張っちゃうし、目立つなあ。
rows.en: Her shirt stretched tight over them. They were hard to miss.

ghs.en: the strain on the fabric is a biiit conspicuous.

rows.jp: なるほど、様子が変なわけだ。
rows.en: No wonder she had been acting so strangely.

rows.jp: 「とりあえず帰って水浴びでもしてきたらどうです？」
rows.en: “Why don’t you go home and take a shower?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "F-, first things first, how about returning home and taking a cold bath?"

variantDisplay.ghsJapanese: 「と、とりあえず帰って水浴びでもしてきたらどうです？」

rows.jp: 「学校の水で、体だけは拭いてるんですけど……」
rows.en: “I wiped myself down with water here at school, but...”

ghs.en: Misato: "But I did rinse my body with the water here at school at least..."

rows.jp: あ、いいなー、そのシチュ。
早起きしてれば遭遇できたのだろうか。
rows.en: If I’d gotten up earlier, could I have walked in on that?

rows.jp: どうしてそういうイベントに流れ着けないかなあ、俺は。
rows.en: Why did I always miss the good stuff?

rows.jp: そういうところが駄目なんだよ。エーロー失格なんだよ。%N※エーロー＝太一語。エロ面における英雄的存在。
rows.en: That was my problem. I was no herotic.%N*Herotic: Taichi-ese. A heroic figure in all matters erotic.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Senpai, please leave this to me!"

rows.en: I went back to the classroom.

rows.jp: 荷物から、スポーツタオルを取り出す。
rows.en: I pulled a sports towel out of my bag.

ghs.en: I take a sports towel from my bag.

rows.jp: 「これで、かわりになりませんか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Would you be able to replace it with this?"

rows.jp: 感動して泣きそうな先輩。
rows.en: Misato looked ready to weep with gratitude.

ghs.en: Senpai is moved and close to tears.

rows.jp: 「サラシってあるでしょう？　あんな感じにすれば、透けないと思いますよ」
rows.en: “You know those cloth wraps people bind their chests with? Wrap this around yourself like one, and nothing should show through.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It is bleached cotton, right? From the feeling of it, I do not think it will become transparent."
ghs.assessment: The source proposes wrapping the towel like a sarashi so the shirt will not show through. The English defines a material, omits the wrapping action, and treats the cloth itself as the thing becoming transparent.
ghs.remedy: Explain that wrapping it like a sarashi should prevent show-through.

highlights.text: It is bleached cotton, right? From the feeling of it, I do not think it will become transparent

rows.en: “You really are such a good boy...”

rows.jp: よよと涙を浮かべつつ、タオルを受け取った。
rows.en: Eyes welling with grateful tears, she accepted the towel.

ghs.en: She accepted the towel while tears flow freely down the cheek.

rows.jp: 「ちょっと待っててくださいね。動いたらめっですよ」
rows.en: “Wait right here. Move and you’re a bad boy.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Wait just a little while now. If you move you get a nai-nai!"
ghs.assessment: The source uses a baby-talk scolding equivalent to 'no-no' if he moves. Leaving an invented romanization in English obscures both the warning and its teasing register.
ghs.remedy: Use a recognizable baby-talk scolding such as 'no-no.'

rows.jp: めっ、されたい気分もあるが、我慢した。
rows.en: Part of me wanted to hear her call me a bad boy, but I resisted.

ghs.en: I did feel I wanted to have this 'nai-nai', but I endured.
ghs.assessment: The narrator repeats the same baby-talk scolding term. The unexplained romanization again withholds its meaning and comic register.
ghs.remedy: Repeat the same intelligible English baby-talk term.

rows.jp: どんなめっ、なのだろう。
rows.en: What kind of “bad boy” did she have in mind?

ghs.en: What kind of 'nai-nai' is that, even.

rows.jp: 寄せた乳房の先端、二粒の野いちごでもって先走る竿の先端を「めっ」と……。
rows.en: She’d squeeze her breasts together, and the two wild strawberries at their tips would scold the precum-slick head of my cock: “Bad boy...”

ghs.en: Udder cusps squeezed together, and with their two wild strawberries on top they approach the tip of an impertinent flagpole, and as a salute, 'nai-nai'...
ghs.assessment: The source's fantasy uses human-body metaphors for breasts and an aroused, pre-ejaculating penis. The English dehumanizes the breasts as udders and mistakes the physiological modifier for a personality judgment about a flagpole.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the human erotic metaphors and the physiological meaning without inventing animal anatomy or insolence.

rows.jp: 「ああああ、ばかばかばか！　俺のばかっ！」
rows.en: “Idiot, idiot, idiot! I’m such an idiot!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "AAAAAH, stupidstupidstupid! You are so stupid!"
ghs.assessment: The source ends the outburst by calling the narrator himself an idiot. The English redirects that final accusation to another person.
ghs.remedy: Keep the self-reproach: 'I'm such an idiot!'

rows.jp: 「やー、ぺけくん、おはようございますっ！！」
めちゃくちゃ晴れやかな顔で現れた。

ghs.en: She came back with a ridiculously cheerful face.
And with her chest proudly puffing,

rows.jp: 「今日も夏日ですね。まだまだ暑さは続きそうです」
rows.en: “Hot again today. Looks like this weather will be with us for a while yet.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Today is another Summer day, is it not! That warmth just continues on and on!"

ghs.assessment: The source is a stammered, polite agreement, roughly 'W-well, quite.' The English idiom instead emphatically denies the proposition and adds profanity, reversing polarity and register.
ghs.remedy: Use a stammered formal agreement such as 'W-well, quite.'

rows.jp: 「それで、今朝はどうしました？」
rows.en: “Now, what brings you here this morning?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Well then, what are you here for on this morning?"
ghs.assessment: The time phrase is ungrammatical in English. The source simply asks what brought him there that morning.
ghs.remedy: Use 'this morning' without 'on.'

rows.jp: 「昨日依頼された原稿をお届けに参りました」
rows.en: “I have come to deliver the manuscript you commissioned yesterday.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I impose to deliver the hand-written script requested of me yesterday."
ghs.assessment: The verb phrase is not idiomatic English and makes the delivery action difficult to parse. The source formally says he has come to deliver the manuscript requested the previous day.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I've come to deliver the manuscript you requested yesterday.'

rows.jp: 「原稿？　初回放送用の台本、書いてくれたんですか？」
rows.en: “The manuscript? You wrote the script for our first broadcast?”

ghs.en: Misato: "A script? You have written a scenario for use in the maiden broadcast?"

rows.jp: 「ぺけくん、すごいです。見違えました」
rows.en: “Peke, that’s amazing. I hardly recognize you.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Peke-kun, that is amazing! That is beyond recognition!"
ghs.assessment: The source praises the addressee with an idiom meaning she can hardly recognize how much he has improved. The English demonstrative instead appears to describe the manuscript as unrecognizable.
ghs.remedy: Make the addressee explicit, for example 'I hardly recognize you.'

rows.jp: 表情は好意と感嘆で満ちている。
rows.en: Her face shone with admiration and delight.

ghs.en: Her face is full of goodwill and admiration.

rows.jp: 俺はロールパンのようにくねくねした。
rows.en: I squirmed like a dinner roll.

ghs.en: I twisted around like a bread roll.

ghs.assessment: The source formally presents the manuscript: 'Here it is.' The English instead expresses willingness or pleasure and omits the presentation action.
ghs.remedy: Use a formal presentation such as 'Here it is.'

ghs.en: I hand her the writing paper.

rows.jp: 先輩の瞳が、きっと厳しさを増す。

ghs.en: Senpai's very pupils sternly grow in severity.
ghs.assessment: The English construction is unidiomatic and redundantly literal. The source says the senior's gaze or eyes grow distinctly sterner as she reads.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai's gaze steadily grew sterner.'

rows.jp: 用紙の上を軽やかに視線は走った。
rows.en: Her gaze flew over the pages.

ghs.en: Her gaze ran light over the script paper.
ghs.assessment: The adverb is malformed in English. The source depicts her gaze moving lightly or briskly across the manuscript.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Her gaze ran lightly over the manuscript.'

ghs.assessment: The source makes Senpai the agent who raises her face or looks up. The English makes her face act independently.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai looked up.'

rows.jp: 満面の笑み。たとえるならば……聖母。
rows.en: A radiant smile. If I had to compare it to anything... the Madonna.

ghs.en: Her entire face is a smile. It was like, to make a comparison... the Virgin Mary.
Like an apparition of the Virgin Mary.

rows.jp: 後光を背負って、彼女は言った。
rows.en: A halo blazing behind her, she spoke.

ghs.en: Her areolar halo a burden, this is what she said:
ghs.assessment: The source says she spoke with a halo or radiance behind her. The English introduces an anatomical sense of 'areolar' and an unsupported burden, corrupting the image.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With a halo shining behind her, she said:'

rows.jp: 柵ごしに、俺は街に吠えた。
rows.en: Through the railing, I howled at the city below.

ghs.en: Through and over the fence I howled at the town.

ghs.assessment: The source is an encouraging 'I'm looking forward to it' or 'I'm counting on you.' The English is an unnatural calque that can imply mere prediction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm looking forward to it.'

rows.jp: すごすごと校舎に戻る。
rows.en: I slunk back toward the school building.

ghs.en: Dejected I return to inside the building.
ghs.assessment: The directional phrase is ungrammatical. The source says he trudges dejectedly back into the school building.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I trudged dejectedly back into the school building.'

rows.jp: 「あ、そうそう、タオルは決して洗わずに返してくださいね」
rows.en: “Oh, one more thing. Please return that towel without washing it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, yes, right, absolutely do not wash that towel before you return it, please."

rows.jp: と、先輩が小首をかしげた瞬間。
rows.en: At the instant she cocked her head—

ghs.en: And, the very instant that Senpai tilted her neck,
ghs.assessment: The literal body-part choice is unnatural and changes the conventional gesture. The source says she cocked or tilted her head.
ghs.remedy: Use 'cocked her head.'

rows.jp: 立てかけてあった様々な資材が、ゆっくりと動き出した。
rows.en: the various construction materials propped nearby began to shift.

ghs.en: all the materials that had been propped up began slowly to move.
I can't make it in time!

rows.jp: 脚立や鉄針、工具……そんなものが。
rows.en: A stepladder, metal spikes, tools... all of it—

ghs.en: The stepladder, the antenna radiators, the tools... all of them,

rows.jp: 一斉に先輩に降り注ぐ。
rows.en: came raining down on her at once.

ghs.en: all at once poured down upon Senpai.

ghs.assessment: The source narrates the immediate event in simple past: Senpai woke up. The English past perfect incorrectly subordinates it to a later past reference point.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai woke up.'

rows.jp: 「良かった……無事で……心配したです」
rows.en: “Thank goodness... you’re safe... I was so worrieded.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am so glad... you are all right... I was so worried!"

ghs.assessment: The source is an interrupted recollection, 'I think I...' or 'I was sure...' The English substitutes a bare perfect-progressive auxiliary and loses the act of remembering.
ghs.remedy: Use an incomplete recollection such as 'I think I...'

rows.jp: 「ひっく、たいしたことなくて本当に良かったよ……」
rows.en: “Sniff... I’m so glad it wasn’t serious...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Sob! I'm really so happy that this isn't any worse..."
She returns to the topic and says,
ghs.assessment: The source says she returns to her normal, unaffected self before speaking. The English instead claims she returns to the subject of conversation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Returning to her usual self, she says,'

rows.en: “They patched you up and brought you here.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You then received medical services here."
ghs.assessment: The source says she was treated and then brought here. The English relocates the treatment to the present location and omits the transfer.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You were treated and brought here.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "And now, you woke. That is all."
Misato: "So I was injured, was I?
ghs.assessment: The English dialogue lacks its closing quotation mark, leaving the presentation structurally incomplete.
ghs.remedy: Add the closing quotation mark after the question mark.

rows.jp: 腕に巻かれている包帯。

ghs.en: the gauze rolled over her arm,

rows.jp: あちこちに張られた絆創膏。

ghs.en: the bandages affixed in a spread all over.
ghs.assessment: The phrase is not idiomatic English. The source describes adhesive bandages stuck here and there over her body.
ghs.remedy: Use 'adhesive bandages stuck here and there.'

highlights.text: affixed in a spread all over

rows.jp: 「いたたたっ、あちこちが痛い……」
rows.en: “Ow, ow, ow... I hurt all over...”

rows.jp: 「全身に軽い打撲とか、あるんで」
rows.en: “Just a few light bruises all over.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You got light bruises all over, that is why."

rows.jp: 「大事がなくてよかったですよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am really glad there is nothing worse."

rows.jp: 「……ありがとう、ぺけくん。呼びかけてくれて」
rows.en: “...Thank you, Peke. You called out to me.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...thank you, Peke-kun. You called out to me."
Misato: "Well then, to club activities now..."
Taichi: "Nope and nope, don't you move."

rows.jp: 「基本的にはたいしたことないんですけど……」
rows.en: “None of it is serious, really, but...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Fundamentally it is no big thing, but still..."

rows.jp: おもむろにシーツをめくって、スカートもめくった。
rows.en: Slowly, I drew back the sheet, then lifted her skirt.

ghs.en: I slowly and deliberately move the sheets off, and flip the skirt as well.

rows.jp: むちむちした大腿部が露出した。むちむち。
rows.en: Her soft, plump thigh lay exposed. Plump.

ghs.en: A femoral region plump and voluptuous got exposed. Plump and voluptuous.
ghs.assessment: Femoral region preserves the source's deliberately formal 大腿部, and the following phrase retains the comic repetition. The confirmed defect is the unidiomatic word order in A femoral region plump and voluptuous got exposed.
ghs.remedy: Keep the formal anatomical noun and repeated plumpness in grammatical English.

rows.jp: 「ほら、このむちむちした太股のとこ、ちょっとささったとですよ。だから今日は部活の方も休んでご自愛いただいてですね……」
rows.en: “See? Something jabbed you right here in this soft, plump thigh. So no club today. You need to rest and take care of yourself...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Look at this plump and voluptuous thigh, it got all pockmarked! So, today you are taking a break from club activities and taking care of yourself..."
ghs.assessment: The source says the thigh was pierced or pricked a little. 'All pockmarked' invents numerous pits and exaggerates the injury.
ghs.remedy: Use 'it got pricked a little.'

rows.jp: ぱくぱくと口を開閉させる。
rows.en: Her mouth opened and closed like a fish.

ghs.en: Pak-pak, she makes her mouth open and close.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese mimetic is copied into English without an intelligible equivalent. The source depicts her opening and closing her mouth soundlessly.
ghs.remedy: Use an English description such as 'Her mouth opens and closes like a fish's.'

rows.jp: 「うわっ、血が滲んじゃってるな」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whoa, there's blood seeping all 'round here!"

ghs.assessment: The speaker label ends with a period rather than the established dialogue delimiter, creating a visible presentation error.
ghs.remedy: Change 'Taichi.' to 'Taichi:'

ghs.assessment: The source depicts repeated jerky nodding but does not specify exactly two nods. The English adds a precise count without support.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She nods jerkily.'

rows.jp: 包帯を持ってきて、取り替える。
rows.en: I fetched a fresh bandage and changed it.

ghs.en: I bring some gauze and go to refresh.
ghs.assessment: The English leaves 'refresh' without an object and does not clearly state that the bandage is replaced. The source explicitly says he brings a bandage and changes it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I bring a fresh bandage and replace the old one.'

ghs.assessment: The English uses interrogative syntax with declarative punctuation and sounds malformed. The source is an admiring comment on her alluring legs.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What sexy legs you have.'

ghs.en: Misato: "I will be doing this myself!"

rows.jp: 「え、ダメですよ。任せてください」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh, no good! Please leave this to me."

rows.jp: 流れ出てしまうなんて。

ghs.assessment: The source expresses dismay that such beautiful blood is flowing out; it does not say the flow is endless. The English adds unsupported duration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'to think it's flowing out like this.'

rows.jp: 目眩を感じて、目を閉じた。

ghs.en: Feeling dizzy, I close the eyes.
ghs.assessment: English requires a possessive here because the narrator closes his own eyes. The source makes that subject clear.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I close my eyes.'

rows.jp: 世界はいつだって曖昧だ。

ghs.en: The world is always ever so ambiguous.

rows.jp: 蠢くものたちは、触れるだけで赤くなる。
rows.en: All that writhes turns red at a touch.

ghs.en: All these squirming little thingies turn red with just a touch.
ghs.assessment: The diminutive, flippant noun is unsupported by the neutral source phrase for writhing or moving things and weakens the altered-state register.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The writhing things turn red at a touch.'

ghs.en: It's simple. It is a simple thing.

rows.jp: 全ての感覚が強化され、不可視のものが見えるようになる。
rows.en: Every sense sharpens. The invisible comes into view.

ghs.en: All the senses strengthen, so that what is invisible becomes as visible.
ghs.assessment: The comparative particle has no complement and makes the result clause ungrammatical. The source says invisible things become visible.
ghs.remedy: Use 'what is invisible becomes visible.'

rows.jp: 可視光域の幅が変わる。
rows.en: The limits of the visible spectrum shift.

ghs.en: The range of visible light changes.

rows.jp: 視界はぼんやりと霞み、動くものを敏感に察知する。
rows.en: My vision clouds over, yet catches the slightest motion.

ghs.en: Faintly the field of vision hazes, and grows sensitive to all that moves.

rows.jp: 唐突に、自分が何者かを忘れる。
rows.en: Abruptly, I forget what I am.

ghs.en: Abruptly, I forget who or what I am,

rows.jp: 意識が切り替わる感覚。
rows.en: The sensation of consciousness switching over.

ghs.en: and I feel my awareness being completely replaced.
ghs.assessment: The source describes the sensation of consciousness switching modes. The English intensifies this into complete replacement, asserting a stronger ontological change than the text supports.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the sensation of my consciousness switching over.'

ghs.assessment: The source is a verb, 'Move' or 'I move.' The English turns the action into an isolated abstract noun.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I move.'

rows.jp: 身体感覚があいまいだ。
rows.en: My sense of my own body grows indistinct.

ghs.en: All sensations throughout the body are ambiguous.

rows.jp: どこからが自分で、そうでないかがわからない。
rows.en: I can no longer tell where I end and the rest of the world begins.

ghs.en: A sense of self off from somewhere doesn't understand whether it isn't.
ghs.assessment: The English is syntactically incoherent and does not convey the source distinction between self and non-self. The source says he cannot tell where he ends and what is not him begins.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't tell where I end and what isn't me begins.'

highlights.text: A sense of self off from somewhere doesn't understand whether it isn't

rows.en: A red point at the center of my vision.

ghs.en: In the center of the field of vision lies a red point.

ghs.assessment: Interference and white noise are plausible interpretations of ノイズ, but expanding one terse source word into a three-item technical list adds distinctions that the source does not state.
ghs.remedy: Keep the source's single terse noise cue.

rows.jp: 何か現象があったらしい。
rows.en: Some phenomenon seems to have occurred.

ghs.en: There's a phenomenon of sort, it seems.
ghs.assessment: The source says some phenomenon apparently occurred. The English uses present existence instead of a past event and contains an ungrammatical singular phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Apparently, some phenomenon occurred.'

ghs.assessment: The intended meaning remains recoverable, but The details I don't understand leaves an English object unexpressed and reads as though the details themselves cannot understand something.
ghs.remedy: Use I don't understand the details or I don't know the details.

ghs.assessment: In context, the source says the phenomenon cannot be experienced or perceived directly. The English instead asserts that the narrator cannot feel his own body, supplying a different object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't feel it directly.'

rows.jp: 世界と一体化した、その全能感だけがすべてだ。
rows.en: Only one thing remains: the omnipotence of being one with the world.

ghs.en: It has integrated with the world, and that sole feeling of omnipotence is now everything.
ghs.assessment: The source describes the narrator's sense of omnipotence from becoming one with the world. The English assigns the integration to an unexplained 'it' and loses the narrator as experiencer.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That sense of omnipotence from becoming one with the world is everything.'

highlights.text: It has integrated with the world

ghs.en: What could this thing even be...

rows.jp: 世界にあって異質なもの。

ghs.en: There is something heterogeneous in the world.

rows.jp: 俺は錯誤しているんだ。
目に見えるものが一義的に日常であると決めつけている。
rows.en: I assume that everything I see belongs, unequivocally, to ordinary reality.

ghs.en: I have arbitrarily concluded that what I can see is unequivocally the normal everyday.
In truth, that is not the case.

rows.jp: その矛盾が、視野の狭窄と改変をもたらす。
rows.en: That contradiction narrows and distorts my field of vision.

ghs.en: That contradiction brings a stricture and a change of the field of view.
ghs.assessment: Stricture can denote constriction, but it is specialized and miscollocated with a field of view here. The source's narrowing and alteration remain otherwise recognizable.
ghs.remedy: Use narrowing or constriction of the field of view.

rows.jp: 出番を心得た獣が、喜悦に身じろぎをした。
rows.en: The beast, knowing its cue, stirs with delight.

ghs.en: The beast, aware its turn has come, stirred with joy.

rows.jp: 現世とは異なる法則・衝動・配列に従って本能を構築した獣だ。
rows.en: A beast whose instincts are built from laws, impulses, and patterns foreign to this world.

ghs.en:
It's a beast constructed of instincts, abiding by
laws - urges - priorities in contrast with the present age.
ghs.assessment: The source contrasts the beast's laws with those of this world or the mortal world, not with a historical present age. The English changes the axis from ontological difference to time period.
ghs.remedy: Use 'different from those of this world.'

highlights.text: in contrast with the present age

ghs.assessment: The imperative is not idiomatic English. The source commands the self to concentrate or focus its consciousness.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Focus your awareness.'

ghs.assessment: The source commands the self to make out or catch the sound, not merely to listen. The English drops the successful-perception component in the command sequence.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Make it out.'

ghs.assessment: The English word is misspelled.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Decipher.'

rows.jp: 自ら口にしたものと同種の波。
rows.en: A wave like the one I produced with my own mouth.

ghs.en: A wave homogeneous with the ones that come out of the mouth.

rows.jp: 意識が収束する。音とわかれば、翻訳もはやい。
rows.en: Consciousness converges. Once I recognize it as sound, translation is swift.

ghs.en: Consciousness converges. If the sound is understood, translation is also speedy.

ghs.en: Those were the words of Senpai,

ghs.assessment: The English tag question is malformed and punctuated as a statement. The source observes that the addressee is always alone and seeks confirmation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're always alone, aren't you?'

rows.en: “Would you like to join the club with me?”

ghs.en: 『Will you not have club together with me?』
ghs.assessment: The phrase is not idiomatic English and obscures the invitation. The source asks whether he would like to do club activities together or join her club.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Would you like to do club activities together?'

ghs.assessment: The English is syntactically and semantically incoherent. The source simply says the narrator's vision clears.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My vision clears.'

ghs.assessment: The source is an exasperated 'Honestly' or 'Good grief.' The English adds profanity and sharpens the irritation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Honestly...' or 'Good grief...'

ghs.en: This timing it has to have.
ghs.assessment: The English is incoherent. The source laments that the episode is happening at this particular moment, roughly 'Of all times.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Of all times...'

highlights.text: This timing it has to have

rows.jp: 血と夕日の組み合わせは、本当に良くない。
rows.en: Blood and sunsets really do not mix.

ghs.en: Blood and sunset assembled are truly not a good thing.
ghs.assessment: The source refers to the combination of blood and sunset. 'Assembled' incorrectly describes objects deliberately put together and produces an unnatural predicate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The combination of blood and sunset is really bad.'

ghs.assessment: The English is ungrammatical and removes the narrator as experiencer. The source says he feels as though he might cry.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I feel like crying.'

rows.jp: 「いやー、困ったもんですね。わはは」
rows.en: “Boy, what a mess. Ha ha ha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, looks like I troubled you. Wahahah!"
ghs.assessment: The source calls the situation troublesome or a problem. The English instead says the narrator caused the addressee trouble, changing the subject and relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Well, this is a problem, isn't it? Ha ha.'

rows.jp: マイヴィーナス、先輩が泣いていた。

ghs.assessment: The source uses the English possessive loan 'my' as a comic epithet. Rendering it as 'Mai' makes it look like a personal name and loses the possessive meaning.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My Venus, Senpai, was crying.'

rows.jp: 「誰だ！　先輩を泣かしたヤツめ、出てこい！」
rows.en: “Who made Misato cry? Come out and face me!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Who was it! Who is it that made Senpai cry, show yourself!"

rows.en: I took up a barehanded fighting stance.

ghs.en: I take a posture of empty-handedness.
ghs.assessment: The source is an established expression for assuming an unarmed fighting stance. The literal abstraction does not convey that he squares up to fight.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I assume an unarmed fighting stance.'

rows.jp: 「俺のカラデを食らわせてやるぞ！」
rows.en: “I’ll give them a taste of my karade!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "My Karade will make you taste defeat!"
Taichi: "Senpai, by whom were you attacked?!"
Senpai pointed a finger at me.

rows.jp: 「自分に打ち克つのは克己(こっき)って書くくらいで難しいナァー！！」
rows.en: “They don’t call it self-conquest for nothing—beating yourself is hard!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "To surmount the self is nearly as difficult as pronouncing the words 'self control'!!!"
ghs.assessment: The source jokes that overcoming oneself is so difficult the written word for self-control literally contains the characters for conquering oneself. The English replaces the orthographic joke with pronunciation and changes the comparison.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the writing-based wordplay, with a concise note if needed.

rows.jp: 「あ、いつものぺけくんに戻ってる……」

ghs.en: Misato: "Ah, the Peke-kun of always has returned..."
ghs.assessment: The noun phrase is an ungrammatical calque. The source says he has returned to his usual self.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah, the usual Peke-kun is back...'

highlights.text: the Peke-kun of always has returned

rows.jp: 「永久にあなたの愛王子であるところの太一です」

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Tis Taichi, eternally the Prince of Your Love."

ghs.assessment: The source narrates the action 'I kneel.' The English gives only a prepositional fragment and does not state the action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I kneel.'

rows.jp: 「ワタクシメのカラデがご入り用ですか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Dost ye have need of your worthless servant's Karade?"
ghs.assessment: The deliberately grandiose register can be preserved, but this auxiliary-pronoun combination is ungrammatical: 'dost' takes 'thou,' while 'ye' takes 'do.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Dost thou...' or 'Do ye...'

rows.jp: 「カラデとかいうわけのわからない格闘技はどうでもいいのですが……」
rows.en: “I don’t care about that incomprehensible martial art you call karade...”

ghs.en: Misato: "That martial art of meaning incomprehensible you call Karade is quite beside the point, however..."
ghs.assessment: The modifier is ungrammatical English. The source calls Karade an incomprehensible martial art.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That incomprehensible martial art you call Karade...'

rows.jp: 「さっきのぺけくん、ロボディアンみたいになってて、恐かったです」%N※ロボディアン＝見里語。ロボットの意。
rows.en: “For a moment, you turned into some kind of robodroid. It scared me.”%N*Robodroid: Misato-ese for “robot.”

ghs.assessment: The complement requires 'like' in English. The source means 'Something like that.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Something like that.'

ghs.assessment: The canonical source assigns this question to the other speaker. The English speaker label attributes it to Taichi and reverses who checks on whom.
ghs.remedy: Assign the line to Misato.

rows.jp: 深くは突っ込まれなかった。
rows.en: She did not press me for details.

rows.en: “Yes. The change of my dual-booted Me-OS has already quicked to THE END, therefore.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, for the changeover of Dual Boot mai OS is now The Endo in Quickly."

rows.jp: 「橋崎先生にぺけくんは英語の成績がひどいと聞いていました」
rows.en: “Mr. Hashizaki told me how terrible your English grades were.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I did hear from Hashisaki-sensei that your grades in English were terrible, Peke-kun."
